verdict.rationale: ByteAsk is itself a coding agent, which would normally make an MCP-server story 'na'. However, the ByteAsk GitHub org publishes an official MCP server (ByteAsk-Embedded-MCP) that other coding agents connect to, so the axis applies. That server only serves page-cited answers from embedded/firmware reference docs; it does not expose the ByteAsk agent itself, and the evidence is a one-line repo description. Missing for 10: an MCP server exposing ByteAsk's core agent capabilities, documented setup/tool list/auth, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: Page-cited answers from embedded & firmware reference docs — for coding agents that can't afford to guess a register value.
